$comment: PHASE 12 POINT 4 — canonical RAW-SCHEMA OWNERSHIP MANIFEST. Every database object here is owned by hand-written migration SQL rather than by the Prisma datamodel. Registering them is what makes the schema authority single and explicit: the datamodel owns table/column EXISTENCE (0 residual differences), and this manifest owns the index-naming, index/FK/unique declarations, column defaults and extension-conditional objects that the datamodel deliberately does not declare. This file is NOT a filter — `scripts/raw-schema-verify.mjs` recomputes the residual set against a fresh database and fails if it differs from this manifest in EITHER direction, so a deleted or mutated registered object is detected, and a NEW undeclared object is detected too.
generatedFrom: prisma migrate diff --from-config-datasource --to-schema, against a fresh PostgreSQL 16 built from the complete migration history (including 20271112000000_point4_write_unblock_repair and 20271117000000_point4_schema_authority_contract). PHASE 12 POINT 6 — enum scopes are now parsed and verified too.

invariants.$note: Both are ZERO by construction: every previously-undeclared live table and column is now declared in schema.prisma. If either becomes non-zero, the datamodel has lost an object the database still has, and the verifier fails.

INDEX_NAME_CONVENTION.reason: Hand-written migrations name indexes with the project convention (e.g. `evidence_ocr_text_team_evidence_idx`); Prisma would generate its own name from the column list. The index itself is semantically identical — same table, same columns, same order. Only the identifier differs.
INDEX_NAME_CONVENTION.risk: none — no data, no constraint semantics

INDEX_DECLARATION.reason: Index created by hand-written migration SQL and deliberately not declared in the datamodel. Prisma never needs it to read or write; the database plans with it.
INDEX_DECLARATION.risk: none — dropping is never proposed against a live table because the datamodel does not claim the table's index set is complete

UNIQUE_DECLARATION.reason: Unique constraint enforced in the database by migration SQL. The runtime relies on the DATABASE to enforce it (see the concurrency integration suites), not on a datamodel declaration.
UNIQUE_DECLARATION.risk: MEDIUM — a dropped unique constraint would be a real integrity loss, which is exactly why the verifier fingerprints it

FOREIGN_KEY_DECLARATION.reason: Referential integrity enforced in the database. Several of these are on raw-SQL-owned subsystem tables whose models declare scalars only (no Prisma relations), so Prisma has no FK to emit.

COLUMN_DEFAULT_DECLARATION.reason: Column default set by migration SQL and not restated in the datamodel. The database applies it on INSERT regardless of what Prisma declares.

COLUMN_TYPE_DECLARATION.reason: Native type detail (varchar length, enum-vs-text) that the datamodel expresses more loosely than the physical column. The physical type is authoritative and unchanged.

ENUM_VARIANT_DECLARATION.reason: Enum variant present in the database type but not restated in the datamodel enum.

EXTENSION_CONDITIONAL_COLUMN.reason: `evidence_semantic_chunks.embedding_vector` is `vector(1536)`, created only when the pgvector extension installs successfully. Migration 20270701000000_phase15_semantic_search installs it best-effort and RAISES NOTICE (never fails) when the host forbids it; semantic search falls back to keyword-only. The column is therefore legitimately absent on a stock postgres:16-alpine and present on a pgvector-enabled host.
EXTENSION_CONDITIONAL_COLUMN.risk: none — the runtime degrades honestly; see the extension manifest below

EXTENSION_CONDITIONAL_INDEX.reason: The ivfflat indexes over the pgvector columns — `evidence_semantic_chunks.embedding_vector` and `evidence_search_documents.embedding`. Prisma cannot express the ivfflat access method, so the datamodel never declares them and raw SQL in the semantic-search migrations creates them alongside the extension. They are the MIRROR of EXTENSION_CONDITIONAL_COLUMN: a conditional column is a divergence exactly while the extension is ABSENT, and a conditional index is a divergence exactly while it is PRESENT. PHASE 12 POINT 5 registered them because it made pgvector a production prerequisite — before that, every rehearsal ran on a host without the extension and neither index had ever existed to diverge.
EXTENSION_CONDITIONAL_INDEX.risk: none — the index is a query-planner accelerator, and its absence degrades semantic search to a sequential scan rather than changing a result

ENUM_LABEL_RESIDUAL.reason: A superseded enum variant that migration history created and the datamodel no longer declares. Prisma only maps DECLARED variants, so an undeclared label is inert for reads and writes UNLESS a row still carries it. Removing one is a CONTRACT step: it requires proof that no row uses the label, so it is registered here with an explicit removal condition rather than dropped to make a diff clean.

PARTIAL_INDEX_DECLARATION.reason: A PARTIAL index — `CREATE INDEX … WHERE <predicate>` — created by hand-written migration SQL. The Prisma schema language has NO syntax for an index predicate: `@@index([field], where: …)` is a validation error, so the datamodel cannot declare this object faithfully. Declaring the column list WITHOUT the predicate would be strictly worse than not declaring it, because `prisma migrate diff` does not compare `pg_index.indpred` at all — it reports a TOTAL index and a PARTIAL index over the same column as identical. The divergence would vanish from this verifier while the datamodel quietly claimed ownership of an object it cannot see, and the next datamodel-derived baseline would emit an UNFILTERED `CREATE INDEX` covering every NULL row. Registering it here keeps one authority and one truth: raw SQL creates it, only a forward migration may change it, and this verifier fails in both directions if it is dropped or its column list changes.
PARTIAL_INDEX_DECLARATION.risk: none for correctness — a partial index bounds index size and accelerates the planner; it enforces no constraint and changes no result. Its LOSS is nevertheless detected, because the entry is verified in both directions. Its PREDICATE is invisible to `migrate diff`, so the predicate is pinned by the source-contract test in `test/phase-12-point4-raw-schema-ownership.test.ts` rather than left unheld.

objects.note: PHASE 12 CORRECTIVE PASS §5.2 (ARCH-002, 2026-08-06) — teams_one_personal_space_per_owner_uk, a PARTIAL unique index (WHERE workspace_kind = 'PERSONAL') created by 20271125000000. Prisma cannot express a partial index in the datamodel, so the introspection diff reports the whole index as unregistered. It enforces the one-Personal-Space-per-identity invariant the workspace-kind backfill classifies from, which is why it is a constraint and not a convention. Owned by the migration; never drop it without also removing the backfill rule that depends on it.

objects.reason: required Automation retry/lease/idempotency index — the sweep's "what is due?" scan, ordered so a retry scheduled into the future cannot starve a fresh run. PARTIAL, so it stays small next to a table whose overwhelming majority of rows are terminal; Prisma cannot express the predicate.

required Automation retry/lease/idempotency index — the reconciler's "whose lease expired?" scan, which is how a run stranded by a dead worker is found instead of staying RUNNING forever. PARTIAL; Prisma cannot express the predicate.

objects.reason: required Automation retry/lease/idempotency index — the constraint that makes a REPLAYED source event collapse to one run per rule. It is what lets the producer use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING inside the caller's transaction instead of catching a violation that would poison it. PARTIAL so historical rows, which legitimately have no source event, are untouched; Prisma cannot express a partial unique index.

required Automation retry/lease/idempotency index — TWO partial indexes on the same column, which the residual diff reports as one line because it compares column sets rather than predicates. They are deliberately separate: the retry pass claims and RESENDS, the ambiguity reconciler must never do so, and an AMBIGUOUS delivery must therefore never share the retry pass's scan.

required Automation retry/lease/idempotency index — finds deliveries abandoned mid-flight by a dead worker. Without it a DELIVERING row left by a crash is indistinguishable from one in flight and is never reclaimed. PARTIAL; Prisma cannot express the predicate.
